samples.question: The picture shows one solid black measuring stick near the top and five horizontal rods below it. The rods all begin on the same left edge and have the same thickness. Four rods are coloured red, green, blue and orange; the fifth rod is grey. The grey rod is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely. Imagine cutting each coloured rod from its left end into pieces exactly as long as the black stick, taking as many whole stick lengths as will fit. What is left over at the right end of that rod, a piece shorter than the black stick, is that rod's LEFTOVER. A rod that is a little longer than three sticks has a short leftover; a rod that is a little shorter than three sticks has a long leftover, so a longer rod does not mean a longer leftover. Nothing is drawn to mark where the cuts would fall; the stick length and the rod lengths are the only measurements needed. In every picture each coloured rod is longer than the black stick, no two coloured leftovers are equal, and no coloured rod is close to an exact whole number of stick lengths. The colours, the vertical order of the rods, the position of the black stick and the number of whole cuts carry no information; the answer need not be the longest rod, need not be the rod that reaches furthest right, and is never the grey rod. Which coloured rod has the longest leftover? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
